D1_decision_equality.phase_A_definition: MethodRegistry::route with MethodChoice::General(policy) returns exactly the decision of GeneralOde::select(problem, options, policy) because it calls it.

grid.identity: the exhaustive decision grid of crates/vigilode/tests/default_path_golden.rs::decision_grid, re-enumerated in the same order by the contract test
grid.entries_formula: 128 feature rows * 12 option rows * 4 dimensions * 36 policies

D1_decision_equality.equality: For every entry: the canonical JSON (sorted keys) of the serde record of the returned selection, or of the returned refusal, of route(General) equals the one of GeneralOde::select. In addition every entry is compared with the decoded golden file crates/vigilode/tests/golden/default_path/decision_grid.json (table 'select'), so the comparison does not rest on the live function alone.
D1_decision_equality.zero_callbacks: Every callback of every grid problem (rhs, dense/band Jacobian, JVP, time derivative, event function) increments one shared atomic counter; the counter must read 0 after all route and select calls.
D1_decision_equality.pass: 221184 of 221184 entries equal against select AND against the golden file, and the callback counter is 0.

phase_B.condition: GeneralOde::select is switched to the registry-derived selection only if the registry-derived selection equals the old body on (i) the 221184-entry golden grid and (ii) the extension grid below, with zero callbacks; the old body then stays in the crate as the test oracle. Otherwise the node stays at phase A and the differing cases are reported.
phase_B.extension_grid: the golden grid with two more Jacobian providers that the golden grid does not enumerate: SparseJvp with a banded pattern (tridiagonal) and SparseJvp with a non-banded pattern (tridiagonal plus one far off-diagonal entry); 6 providers * 32 feature rows * 12 option rows * 4 dimensions * 36 policies = 331776 entries. It is called 'extension grid', never 'golden grid'.
phase_B.equality: same canonical-JSON equality, registry-derived selection against the retained old body.
phase_B.golden_check: crates/vigilode/tests/default_path_golden.rs must pass unchanged after the switch (it calls GeneralOde::select).

starter_error_control_rule.why_adapter_side: crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/ppsw1.rs is protected; ppsw1::start is one 5-stage Radau IIA step over [t0, t0 + 2 h0] with no error estimate.
starter_error_control_rule.estimate: Step doubling on the adapter side. F = start(t0, y0, h0). A = start(t0, y0, h0/2) covers the first half, B = start(t0 + h0, A.y[5], h0/2) the second half. Reference values at the five non-initial nodes of F (fractions 1/4, 1/2, 7/10, 9/10, 1 of the interval): A.y[2], A.y[5], the degree-5 polynomial through the six node values of B evaluated at local fractions 0.4 and 0.8, and B.y[5]. est = max over the five nodes of ppsw1::error_norm(F.y[k], F.y[k] - ref_k, atol, rtol) with the caller's tolerances.
starter_error_control_rule.decision: accept F iff est <= 1 (ppsw1::accepts). Otherwise h0 <- h0/2, F <- A (reused, not recomputed) and the estimate is repeated; at most 40 halvings, then a typed failure. A callback or solver error inside any of the three starter solves stops the run with a typed reason.
starter_error_control_rule.nature: an estimate, not a bound (Richardson-type comparison: the half-step references carry about 1/64 of the interior and 1/512 of the endpoint error of F).
starter_error_control_rule.work: every starter solve is charged to startup_work.
starter_error_control_rule.search_budget: none: the constants are fixed here and are not tuned on the results.

peer_defects.regression_check_exploratory: Before the fix, FNV-1a digests of the PeerOde trajectories (times and states) of the four U07 cases (Prothero-Robinson, dense and JVP provider, threads 1 and 4, rtol 1e-8, atol 1e-10, h0 rule cap 0.01) are recorded on the base sources. After the fix the digests are compared: equality means the starter control accepted the first h0 and left the accepted trajectory bit for bit unchanged (startup work counters grow by the two control solves). auto_policy.opt_in: MethodChoice::Auto is never a default (owner decision OD-L1-3). GeneralOde, Rodas5p and every other existing frontend keep their behaviour.
auto_policy.ranking: Candidates are the registry entries whose adapter is available and whose admission for the declared facts and the caller's capability set succeeds. Order: (1) regime fit (declared stiff: implicit methods before explicit ones; declared nonstiff or unknown: explicit before implicit), (2) qualification (production, scoped calibration, implemented-unqualified, reference-only), (3) registry order. The whole ranking with every refusal reason is returned in the plan.
auto_policy.measured_evidence: Used only when the policy says so and only as data supplied by the caller (selection_evidence::CostEvidence per method with the callback units spent to obtain it); route stays pure. The supplied callback units are added to the work summary of the solution. No evidence is measured by route.
auto_policy.fallback: Off unless the policy enables it. When enabled, a failed attempt is followed by the next ranked candidate, restarted at t0 (no state of the failed attempt is reused). Every attempt is kept with its route id, typed failure, accepted prefix and work; the total work includes failed attempts.
auto_policy.no_performance_claim: This node makes no claim that Auto is faster or more accurate than any explicit choice.

exclusion_rules: None. Every executed contract case is reported; failed and negative runs stay in the logs.
